newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-RUSSIAN PREMIER LOBBIES FOR ST PETERSBURG BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-RUSSIAN PREMIER LOBBIES FOR ST PETERSBURG BID.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin joined government and Russian Olympic officials over the past two days urging International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch to award the 2004 Games to St Petersburg.
At a news conference on Sunday, Samaranch said the Russian premier had "insistently laid out the arguments for St Petersburg".

Russia's former tsarist capital, an industrial city of five million, is one of 11 candidates vying for the 2004 Games. The others are Rome, Cape Town, Stockholm, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Buenos Aires, Athens, Lille, Seville and Istanbul.

"St Petersburg is a legendary city, world famous and very beautiful," Samaranch said. "In 2004, I will no longer be IOC president but, if I am living, I will gladly come to St Petersburg for the Olympic Games."
The Russian government has promised a huge cash injection and argued that the Games would be an international endorsement of the country's transition to democracy.
